discovery: Invention and development of atom interferometry as a precision tool for inertial sensing and fundamental physics

nominees.name: Christian J. Bordé
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique des Lasers, Université Sorbonne Paris Nord / SYRTE, Observatoire de Paris, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Matter-wave interferometry with atoms has become one of the most sensitive measurement techniques in physics. Bordé recognized that the momentum recoil of absorbed photons coherently splits atomic wave packets, and he established the theory of the Ramsey-Bordé interferometer. Pritchard's group built the first interferometer for atoms using material nanogratings, which brought coherent atom optics into the laboratory. Kasevich, working with Chu, demonstrated light-pulse atom interferometry with stimulated Raman transitions and then turned it into gravimeters, gyroscopes and gradiometers with record, carefully characterized accuracy. Together their work opened an entirely new measurement capability. Today it yields the most precise determination of the fine-structure constant, measurements of G, tests of the equivalence principle, searches for dark energy and dark matter, and field-deployable quantum inertial sensors. Proposed gravitational-wave detectors are also built on it. The gains are orders of magnitude, and the whole field rests on their foundations.
